content: A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of all possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before taking itraconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages, and discuss marijuana use with your doctor. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. This medication should not be used to treat fungal nail infections if you are pregnant or could become pregnant during treatment. Itraconazole passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Itraconazole interacts with many medications. Other drugs can affect how itraconazole is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests) should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while taking it. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Itraconazole should not be used to treat fungal nail infections if you have a history of heart failure, as it may rarely cause or worsen heart failure. Notify your doctor immediately if you develop symptoms of heart failure, such as shortness of breath, swelling of the ankles or feet, unusual tiredness, or sudden unexplained weight gain. This medication can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially causing very serious (and possibly fatal) side effects. Examples of affected drugs include certain blood thinners (e.g., ticagrelor), colchicine, medications for irregular heartbeat (e.g., disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine), eplerenone, ergot alkaloids (e.g., dihydroergotamine, ergotamine, methylergonovine), felodipine, fesoterodine, irinotecan, ivabradine, lurasidone, methadone, midazolam, nisoldipine, pimozide, ranolazine, certain statin cholesterol drugs (e.g., lovastatin, simvastatin), solifenacin, telithromycin, triazolam, and others. Itraconazole is used to treat a variety of fungal infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as azole antifungals. Follow the instructions provided by your doctor and the patient information leaflet, if available, before starting this medication and with each refill. Take itraconazole by mouth with a full meal, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. Take itraconazole 2 hours before or 1 hour after antacids, as antacids may reduce its absorption. If you have decreased or no stomach acid (achlorhydria) or take medications that reduce stomach acid (e.g., H2 blockers like ranitidine or proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole), take this medication with an acidic drink (e.g., cola). The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Take this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For optimal results, take this antifungal at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) every day. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. The capsule, tablet, and solution forms of this medication deliver different amounts of the drug and may be used for different purposes. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, stomach upset, or dizziness. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Itraconazole has rarely caused very serious (and possibly fatal) liver disease. It may also commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately.
